description: Drawing knowledge is the recorded context around a drawing: revisions, questions, explanations, decisions, approvals and handoffs.

args: The drawing is the file. Drawing knowledge is everything people need to understand it.

The source
The drawing, sheet, detail and applicable revision.
The discussion

The outcome

The next action

The gap appears when the information still exists but the next person cannot reliably connect it to the drawing, revision or decision in front of them.

Common signs include an answer that only one person can find, a visible revision without its explanation, a resolved issue without a usable outcome, or a downstream team receiving the drawing without the conditions that govern it.

sections.heading: Recorded knowledge is not inferred intent

args: A comparison may show that a note changed. It does not prove why the author changed it. The explanation becomes usable knowledge when a responsible person records it or connects the review to an appropriate source.

args: Use a consistent drawing number, revision identifier, sheet identity and package context. Avoid relying on filename order, inbox dates or informal labels such as final and latest.

The revision label does not decide which drawing a job may use. Your change, approval and release process determines applicability and effectivity.

name: Worked Review Example
title: Connected Engineering Drawing Review Example | VizeDraw
description: Follow an illustrative drawing question from its source revision to a recorded response, revised drawing and next action.
purpose: Show the product concept in a concrete, credible scenario.

args: Follow one drawing question from source to outcome.
Illustrative example. The identifiers and participants below are fictional. This is not a customer result or an engineering instruction.

A machinery team is reviewing drawing DEMO-104 Revision A. A supplier asks whether a cover-access note refers to the operator side or the service side. The question matters to the supplier's interpretation, but the drawing note does not provide enough context to answer safely.
The review identifies DEMO-104 Revision A, the marked note and the purpose of the review. The question is not stored as an isolated screenshot without a drawing reference.
Question: Which side is intended by the cover-access note on this revision?
Responsible reviewer: the assigned design-review owner.
Status: awaiting clarification.

The design-review owner consults the responsible product owner. The explanation is recorded in CHANGE-DEMO-07, and the drawing note is updated in Revision B. The software does not invent the designer's intent; a responsible person supplies and records the explanation.
The team reviews the changed note in Revision B and checks whether other affected details need attention. The Revision A question remains part of the history and is connected to the updated source.
Clarification outcome
The intended meaning has been explained and the note updated.
Review evidence
The response and relevant change reference are recorded.
Manufacturing release

name: Company
title: About VizeDraw | Drawing Intelligence by Zenitude
description: Learn why Zenitude is building VizeDraw to keep the knowledge behind engineering drawings connected from design to execution.
purpose: Explain the company, category position and product principles in a concise credible way.

args: Built around the way engineering work actually moves.

VizeDraw is developed by Zenitude for teams whose work depends on engineering drawings. Our focus is the knowledge created around those drawings: what changed, what was questioned, what was accepted and what the next person needs to know.

Manufacturing is the first market focus because drawings move continuously between engineering, suppliers, customers, production and quality. The file may travel successfully while the explanation behind it becomes difficult to recover.
VizeDraw is being built to keep that review context connected from design to execution.
The drawing and its context belong together
Questions, responses and decisions are most useful when their source remains visible.
Information should stay connected to evidence
Missing context should be identified, not replaced with confident assumptions.
AI should assist judgement
Qualified people remain responsible for technical decisions and authorized release.
Evidence matters more than broad promises
Teams should evaluate a real workflow and inspect whether the result is easier to understand and recover.

sections.heading: A focused role in the engineering stack

args: VizeDraw is a Drawing Intelligence Workspace. It is not presented as a replacement for every CAD, PDM, PLM, quality or production system. Start where a focused drawing-review experience can improve the handoff, and keep the systems and controls that already work.
